sentences.1: What if the foot, ordained the dust to tread, or hand, to toil, aspired to be the head?
sentences.2: What if the head, the eye, or ear repined to serve mere engines to the ruling mind?
sentences.3: Just as absurd for any part to claim to be another, in this general frame: just as absurd, to mourn the tasks or pains, the great directing Mind of All ordains.
sentences.4: All are but parts of one stupendous whole, whose body Nature is, and God the soul; that, changed through all, and yet in all the same; great in the earth, as in the ethereal frame; warms in the sun, refreshes in the breeze, glows in the stars, and blossoms in the trees, lives through all life, extends through all extent, spreads undivided, operates unspent; breathes in our soul, informs our mortal part, as full, as perfect, in a hair as heart: as full, as perfect, in vile man that mourns, as the rapt seraph that adores and burns: to him no high, no low, no great, no small; he fills, he bounds, connects, and equals all.
sentences.5: Cease, then, nor order imperfection name: our proper bliss depends on what we blame.
sentences.6: Know thy own point: this kind, this due degree of blindness, weakness, Heaven bestows on thee.
sentences.8: In this, or any other sphere, secure to be as blest as thou canst bear: safe in the hand of one disposing Power, or in the natal, or the mortal hour.
sentences.9: All nature is but art, unknown to thee; all chance, direction, which thou canst not see; all discord, harmony not understood; all partial evil, universal good: and, spite of pride in erring reason's spite, one truth is clear, whatever is, is right.

leftover: Sentence 1: “What if the foot, ordained the dust to tread, or hand, to toil, aspired to be the head?” — What-if question about aspiration and assigned purpose. It supplies neither one admitted ledger change nor a stated THEN proposition; do not turn the question into an actual aspiration.

Sentence 2: “What if the head, the eye, or ear repined to serve mere engines to the ruling mind?” — What-if question about discontent and mind-as-ruler imagery; no stated testable consequent or actual complaint.

Sentence 3: “Just as ... just as; in this general frame; the great directing Mind of All” — Equal-degree comparison, frame/location and divine mind imagery. a/b are evaluations of described actions, not attributions that anyone actually claims or mourns.

Sentence 4: “one stupendous whole; body; soul; great in the earth, as in the ethereal frame; warms in the sun, refreshes in the breeze, glows in the stars, and blossoms in the trees, lives through all life, extends through all extent, spreads undivided, operates unspent; breathes in our soul, informs our mortal part; as full, as perfect; vile man; rapt seraph; no high, no low, no great, no small; fills, bounds, connects, and equals all” — Cosmic body/soul imagery, spatial extent, quantities/perfection and personified divine actions. d/e/f are explicitly marked interpretive relations, not literal anatomy or instantiated physical events. The local contrast between changed and same is not rewritten as an unqualified contradiction.

Sentence 5: “Cease, then, nor order imperfection name; proper; what we blame” — Commands and evaluation/attitude; g retains only the stated dependency, without asserting that bliss has occurred or identifying an action that changes it.

Sentence 6: “Know thy own point; this kind, this due degree; on thee; Heaven” — Command, degree/propriety and divine personification. k/l use the text's bestows under a marked figurative reading; they are not shaped transfers and do not establish a literal bodily press.

Sentence 8: “In this, or any other sphere, secure to be as blest as thou canst bear: safe in the hand of one disposing Power, or in the natal, or the mortal hour.” — Elliptical assurance with possible imperative scope, sphere/hand imagery, degree of blessedness, modality and birth/death timing. No unqualified safety or bodily support event is asserted.

Sentence 9: “but; unknown to thee; which thou canst not see; not understood; spite of pride in erring reason's spite; one truth is clear” — Attitudes, inability to see, rhetorical emphasis and the art/direction/harmony/good transformations. m–p preserve those four identifications as opaque figurative readings, not a physical or mathematical identity proof.

readings: Sentence 4. Open readings: that refers to God, Nature, or the whole. Chosen: divine whole, filled in; identity over changed manifestations is a selected reading, not an emendation.
Sentence 5. Open readings: what we blame denotes people, events or conditions. Chosen: conditions, filled in; no condition is asserted present and no control action is invented.
Sentence 6. Open readings: literal acts of Heaven or personification of allotted limitations. Chosen: personified bestowal, marked filled in; source verb retained and no response class guessed.
Sentence 9. Open readings: literal identities or paradoxical figurative identifications. Chosen: the latter, filled in; no inverse rules or ex-falso reasoning supplied.
Correction 1: whole and divine_whole had denoted the same referent. Use whole everywhere; divine is descriptive, not a second entity.
